transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-08-19 15:00 PDT; Duration: 48 minutes; Attendees listed above.

Summary: Quick partner intro between Redwood and Sequoia Ops (SI). Primary objective: understand Sequoia's managed services offering for hybrid customers, map integration points for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments, discuss security/compliance gating (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and scope a pilot/proof-of-concept for a mid-market customer.

Topics: partner resell model, on-prem GPU provisioning, VPC peering patterns, KMS/HSM integration, pilot success criteria, timeline, pricing/partner margin, technical bench for performance validation.

Resources referenced: Redwood partner deck (link dropped in chat), joint pilot SOW template (to be shared), Sequoia internal network diagram (requested).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round the table, i'll be maya from redwood, diego's our se and lina handles partner ops.
[00:18] Priya (Sequoia): hi, priya here. we run sequoia ops channel partnerships and managed services. ethan and samir from our infra and solution teams. thanks for setting up.
[00:27] Diego (Redwood SE): hey all, diego. excited to dig into the infra detail.
[00:32] Ethan (Sequoia): hi. first time on a call with redwood, we've been hearing nice things about the runtime.
[00:38] Maya: cool. objective today is exploratory. understand your go-to-market for hybrid customers, technical constraints for on-prem GPU installs, and what a pilot looks like.
[00:49] Samir: to be frank, we have several enterprise customers asking for private inference in air-gapped or VPC-only setups. we want to see how redwood's private stack fits into our delivery model. key concerns: latency, ops overhead, and encryption at rest with our KMS.
[01:08] Maya: makes sense. do you typically resell software or do full managed infra?
[01:14] Priya: we do both. some customers want the software installed on their premises and we manage it; for others we provide colocation + mgd services. our pricing is usually a combination of monthly managed fees + infra usage.
[01:27] Diego: okay. for Private deployments we offer the same control plane API but you can host the runtime on your infra. curious about your GPU inventory and whether you support NVIDIA A100 / H100 or other accelerators?
[01:40] Samir: primary fleet is A100s; we have some partners testing H100. but our ops model includes a mix — sometimes customers bring their own or we place racks in partner colo.
[01:51] Ethan: operationally we want predictable throughput; customers often request committed capacity. question: does redwood support reserved capacity semantics in private installs or is that only for hosted?
[02:05] Maya: reserved semantics are supported via Redwood Dedicated in hosted, but we can map similar guarantees in private by reserving GPU pools and configuring autoscaling policies in the customer's infra. needs to be defined in the SOW.
[02:19] Priya: on security, SOC2 is a must for our customers. do you have SOC2 and how do audit logs surface in Private?
[02:30] Diego: yes, redwood is SOC2 and we surface audit logs to the control plane. in Private we support forwarding logs to a customer SIEM or storing locally; also we integrate with SAML SSO and RBAC. small caveat: some air-gapped customers require the control plane to be on-prem too — we have an optional private control plane package.
[02:50] Jordan (Sequoia): i want to call out KMS. customers prefer their KMS/HSM for key material. can redwood use customer-managed KMS for model keys / disk encryption?
[03:03] Maya: yes, we support KMS integrations (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, and on-prem HSMs). there can be some nuances with disk encryption vs model artifact signing but it's supported.
[03:15] Samir: good. another practical question: how does redwood handle model variants and fallbacks? e.g., if high-perf model isn't available on premise, can requests route to hosted or a different quantized variant?
[03:30] Diego: we have smart routing policies. you can define policy to prefer on-prem, fallback to hosted (if allowed), or to use a quantized variant optimized for the available hardware. for strict air-gapped customers fallback is blocked of course.
[03:45] Priya: pricing wise, we need partner margin and reseller terms. do you have an existing partner reseller program?
[03:54] Maya: yes, we have a partner program. we can share partner pricing tiers and margins; typically pilot pricing is discounted and we carve a separate seat for integration & benching. i'll share the template.
[04:07] Ethan: infrastructure questions — do you require specific kernel builds for quantized models? our ops team is sensitive about kernel/custom libs.
[04:18] Diego: good point. we recommend specific builds for best perf; for quantized inference we may need custom operators. we can provide prebuilt runtimes or work with your infra to build. the bench will validate that.
[04:32] Priya: what's the typical timeline for a pilot? some of our customers want a 4 week proof, others want 8.
[04:40] Maya: for a minimal functional pilot (validation of end-to-end inference in your environment plus perf baselines) we usually plan 3-6 weeks depending on access. full validation with security/compliance often takes longer.
[04:51] Samir: about the bench — can you run a micro-bench that includes cost per token estimates at our typical request sizes (avg seq 256, peak seq 1024)?
[05:02] Diego: yes, we'll need sample prompts, expected QPS, and model choices. typical outputs: p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost estimates given your fleet. we'll include KV cash behavior (sic — "K V cash" is sometimes in transcripts) and expected prefix cache saving.
[05:22] Priya: hmm i heard "K V cash" — maybe transcriber misheard, but yes we need KV cache behavior explained. also how does redwood optimize batching vs latency?
[05:33] Diego: we have continuous batching with latency SLO controls. you can set per-route latency targets and the runtime will balance batching size to keep p95/p99 under threshold while maximizing throughput.
[05:47] Jordan: network egress — for colocation installs, do you require outbound for telemetry or can everything be local?
[05:56] Maya: telemetry can be forwarded to your SIEM; control plane pingback optional. for fully air-gapped setups, we offer on-prem control plane. there's a trade-off: remote control plane gives easier upgrades.
[06:08] Samir: can the partner (sequoia) operate the control plane for customers or do you only allow redwood-run control plane?
[06:16] Maya: partners can operate an instance of the private control plane under a partner agreement; there are support and license terms to enable that. it's a common model for SI resellers.
[06:27] Priya: excellent. one of our customers is in regulated finance, wants model auditability, per-call provenance. can redwood provide tracing / token-level cost and a per-request audit trail?
[06:40] Diego: yes, our console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route tracing hooks, and you can export traces to your logging infra. for regulatory customers we can lock retention windows and sign attestations in the SOW.
[06:55] Ethan: any blockers you foresee for a pilot with our standard colo?
[07:01] Diego: nothing major. we'll need runbook access, some SRE time to configure networking and firewall rules, and possibly kernel/operator installs. we'll outline requirements in the pilot plan.
[07:12] Priya: what's your recommended pilot success criteria?
[07:16] Maya: quick list: 1) deploy runtime on Sequoia infra, 2) run predefined benchmark and meet latency/cost targets, 3) integrate KMS and demonstrate keys are customer-managed, 4) complete basic security review and logging export, 5) define go-to-market play and partner margin.
[07:37] Samir: ok. we'll map that to our internal checklist.
[07:41] Maya: next steps (recap) — i'll send pricing template and pilot SOW. diego will draft bench plan and list runtime/kernel requirements. samir to share network diagram. priya to confirm interested customer for pilot.
[07:54] Priya: sounds good. any competitors or specific integrations you think we should highlight?
[07:59] Diego: sometimes we see customers evaluating MegaCloud AI or OrionServe; highlighting Redwood's kernel-level optimizations, quantization guidance and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private is helpful.
[08:13] Jordan: one last quick ops question — upgrades. how are upgrades handled for private control plane?
[08:19] Maya: can be scheduled with partner-managed upgrade windows; we provide upgrade packages and can automate with your CI. for air-gapped, it's manual bundle-based.
[08:29] Ethan: ok. that's it from me, thanks.
[08:33] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the documents.

End: Meeting ended ~48 minutes.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels genericized, filler words present, some acronyms mis-transcribed (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache; "sock two" for SOC2).
